'''Otto Eberhard Rössler''' (20 May 1940 – 5 October 2026) was a German interdisciplinary scientist who worked in theoretical [[biochemistry]] and [[nonlinear physics]]. He was internationally known for his work on [[chaos theory]] and the Rössler [[mathematical model]], whose solution most often tend to a [[strange attractor]] called [[Rössler attractor]]. 

Rössler is best known to the general public for his involvement in a failed lawsuit to halt the [[Large Hadron Collider]] due to fears that it would generate mini black holes.

==Life and career==
Rössler was born in [[Berlin]], into an academic family: his father, also named Otto Rössler, was an Austrian Nazi and a scholar of [[Semitic languages]] who was affiliated with the [[Ahnenerbe]] and later held a professorship at the [[University of Marburg]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YzQNSTvHv-sC&pg=PA300|title=Nazi Propaganda for the Arab World|first=Jeffrey|last=Herf|publisher=Yale University Press|year=2009|isbn=978-0-300-14579-3|page=300}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Geschichte des Faches in Marburg|url=http://www.uni-marburg.de/cnms/semitistik/fachgebiet/history|date=January 21, 2009|language=de|publisher=University of Marburg|access-date=2012-04-21}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Vom Antisemiten zum Semitistik-Professor: Chronologie Rössler, Otto|language=de|first=Gerd|last=Simon|url=http://homepages.uni-tuebingen.de/gerd.simon/ChrRoessler.pdf|access-date=2012-04-21|date=November 2010}}.</ref>

He was awarded his MD in 1966. After postdoctoral studies at the [[Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Physiology]] in [[Bavaria]], and a visiting appointment at the Center for Theoretical Biology at [[University at Buffalo, The State University of New York|SUNY-Buffalo]], in 1969 he became Professor for Theoretical Biochemistry at the [[University of Tübingen]]. In 1994, he became Professor of Chemistry by decree.<ref name="atomosyd">[http://www.atomosyd.net/spip.php?article6 Collaborator profile], ATOMOSYD research group, accessed 2012-04-21.</ref><ref name="science20">{{citation|journal=[[Science 2.0]]|first=Alan|last=Gillis|title=Interview: Professor Otto Rössler Takes On The LHC|date=August 12, 2008|url=http://www.science20.com/big_science_gambles/blog/interview_professor_otto_r%C3%B6ssler_takes_lhc-31449}}.</ref>

Rössler held visiting positions at the [[University of Guelph]] (Mathematics) in [[Canada]], the Center for Nonlinear Studies of the [[University of California]] at Los Alamos, the [[University of Virginia]] (Chemical Engineering), the [[Technical University of Denmark]] (Theoretical Physics), and the [[Santa Fe Institute]] (Complexity Research) in [[New Mexico]].<ref name="atomosyd"/><ref name="science20"/>

Rössler died on 5 October 2026, at the age of 86.<ref>{{cite web |title=Otto E. Rössler |url=https://www.trauer.swp.de/traueranzeige/otto-e-roessler |website=SWP Trauer |access-date=28 October 2026}}</ref>

==Research==
Rössler authored hundreds of scientific papers in fields as wide-ranging as [[biogenesis]], the [[origin of language]], differentiable automata, chaotic attractors, [[endophysics]], micro relativity, artificial universes, the hypertext encyclopedia, and world-changing technology.

His most heavily cited publication is the 1976 paper<ref>{{citation | last = Rössler | first = O. E. | doi = 10.1016/0375-9601(76)90101-8 | issue = 5 | journal = [[Physics Letters|Physics Letters A]] | pages = 397–398 | title = An equation for continuous chaos | volume = 57 | year = 1976}}.</ref> in which he studied what is now known as the [[Rössler attractor]], the [[strange attractor]] of a system of three differential equations that exhibit [[chaos theory|chaotic dynamics]].<ref>{{citation | last1 = Peitgen | first1 = Heinz-Otto | author1-link = Heinz-Otto Peitgen | last2 = Jürgens | first2 = Hartmut | author2-link = Hartmut Jürgens | last3 = Saupe | first3 = Dietmar | author3-link = Dietmar Saupe | contribution = 12.3 The Rössler Attractor | pages = 636–646 | publisher = Springer| title = Chaos and Fractals: New Frontiers of Science | year = 2004}}.</ref><ref>{{citation | last1 = Letellier | first1 = C. | last2 = Dutertre | first2 = P. | last3 = Maheu | first3 = B. | doi = 10.1063/1.166076 | issue = 1 | journal = Chaos | pages = 272–281 | title = Unstable periodic orbits and templates of the Rössler system: toward a systematic topological characterization | volume = 5 | year = 1995| doi-access = free }}.</ref> Rössler discovered his system after a series of exchanges with [[Arthur Winfree]] as detailed by {{harvtxt|Letellier|Messager|2010}}.<ref>{{citation | last1 = Letellier | first1 = C. | last2 = Messager | first2 = V. | doi = 10.1142/S0218127410027854 | issue = 11 | journal = International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos | pages = 3585–3616 | title = Influences on Otto E. Rössler's earliest paper on chaos | volume = 20 | year = 2010}}</ref> In 2015, Rössler published in ''[[Progress in Biophysics and Molecular Biology]]'' "a journal article that points not only to a potential cure for autism, but also a means of creating mystical, all-wise elephants".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thecut.com/2015/07/mystical-elephants-theory-of-autism.html|title=Here’s a Peer-Reviewed Article That Suggests a Method for Curing Autism and Creating Mystical Elephants|work=The Cut|last=Singal|first=Jesse|date=July 7, 2015}}</ref>

==Advocacy==
Rössler and his wife, Reimara, were involved with a long-running series of disputes with their employer, the University of Tübingen, which they accused of discrimination and of violations of academic freedom.<ref>Wolf Schmidt: [http://www.taz.de/1/zukunft/wissen/artikel/1/der-prophet-des-planetentods/ Der Prophet des Planetentods] [[die tageszeitung]], 8 September 2008</ref> In 1988, Reimara Rössler, a professor of medicine, was transferred to a different department within the university; in protest, she began working from home. The state of [[Baden-Württemberg]] sued her for failure to perform her assigned duties, as a result of which by 1996 she lost her job and was forced to give up a second home to refund her back pay. Meanwhile, in 1993 and 1994, Otto Rössler had been assigned to teach an introductory chemistry course according to the prescribed curriculum for medical students, but insisted instead on teaching his own material. After he was replaced in the course by another lecturer, he continued trying to give the lectures himself, and was removed by police several times. Because of these incidents, in 1995 a state official tried to force Rössler to undergo psychological tests, but after international protests by many academics this plan was dropped. Rössler continued protesting against his and his wife's treatment by the university and in August 2001 he was caught defacing the university auditorium with spray paint in an attempt to draw attention to his protests.<ref>{{citation|title=Lizenz fürs Chaos: Ein Tübinger Professor weigert sich, eine Chemievorlesung für Anfänger zu halten|date=January 9, 1995|first=Rainer|last=Frick|url=http://www.focus.de/politik/deutschland/universitaet-lizenz-fuers-chaos_aid_151161.html|language=de|journal=[[Focus (German magazine)|Focus]]}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.focus.de/magazin/archiv/hochschulen-chaosforscher-muss-zum-psycho-test_aid_151227.html|title=Chaosforscher muß zum Psycho-Test|date=March 27, 1995|language=de|journal=[[Focus (German magazine)|Focus]]}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Der Chaosforscher und die Windmühlenflügel|journal=[[Der Spiegel]]|date=August 29, 2001|first=Jochen|last=Leffers|language=de|url=http://www.spiegel.de/unispiegel/studium/0,1518,151581,00.html}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Tragische Gestalt|journal=[[Der Spiegel]]|date=September 15, 2001|first=Caroline|last=Von Schmidt|language=de|url=http://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/d-20128744.html}}.</ref>

In June 2008, Rössler publicly criticized the [[Large Hadron Collider]] experiment supervised by [[CERN]] in [[Geneva]] and was involved in a failed lawsuit to halt it. He argued that the experiment could plausibly generate dangerous miniature black holes that could bring about the end of the world.<ref name="science20"/><ref name="telegraph">{{citation|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/2650665/Legal-bid-to-stop-CERN-atom-smasher-from-destroying-the-world.html|title=Legal bid to stop CERN atom smasher from 'destroying the world'|access-date=2012-02-04|first=Richard|last=Gray|date=28 April 2010|publisher=[[Daily Telegraph]]}}</ref> Hermann Nicolai, director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]]' quantum gravity division, later described Rössler's arguments as being "...&nbsp;based on an elementary misunderstanding of the theory of general relativity".<ref>{{citation|first=Hermann|last=Nicolai|title=Comments on speculations raised by Professor Otto Rössler about the production of black holes at the LHC|date=July 2008|url=http://environmental-impact.web.cern.ch/environmental-impact/Objects/LHCSafety/NicolaiComment-en.pdf|publisher=[[CERN]]|access-date=2012-02-04|archive-date=2018-11-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181107110445/http://environmental-impact.web.cern.ch/environmental-impact/Objects/LHCSafety/NicolaiComment-en.pdf|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

Rössler was also an honorary editor of the journal ''[[Elsevier#Chaos, Solitons & Fractals|Chaos, Solitons & Fractals]]'', which came under fire in 2009 for allegedly publishing papers without as strict [[peer review]] as would be expected for a scientific journal. In a subsequent libel suit brought by former journal editor [[Mohammed El Naschie]] in response to this criticism, Rössler testified on behalf of El Naschie, stating in court about peer review that "if you have something new to offer, peer review is dangerous", adding that in such cases "peer review delays progress in science".<ref>{{citation|title=Nature journal libel case continues|first=Pallab|last=Ghosh|journal=[[BBC News]]|date=25 November 2011|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-15889634}}.</ref>

==Books==
Rössler was the author or co-author of:
* ''Encounter with Chaos: Self-Organized Hierarchical Complexity in Semiconductor Experiments'' (with J. Peinke, J. Parisi, and R. Stoop 1992, Springer-Verlag, 1992, <small>{{ISBN|0-387-55647-8}}</small>)
* ''Das Flammenschwert oder wie hermetisch ist die Schnittstelle des Mikrokonstruktivismus?'' (in German, Benteli, 1996, <small>{{ISBN|3-7165-1017-3}}</small>)
* ''Interventionen. Vertikale und horizontale Grenzüberschreitung'' (in German, with René Stettler, Stroemfeld, 1997, <small>{{ISBN|3-87877-627-6}}</small>)
* ''Aussenwelt – Innenwelt – Überwelt. Ein Gespräch'' (in German, with René Stettler and Peter Weibel, Stroemfeld, 1997, <small>{{ISBN|3-87877-628-4}}</small>)
* ''Endophysics: The World As An Interface'' (World Scientific, 1998, <small>{{ISBN|981-02-2752-3}}</small>)
* ''Das Denken eines Kindes: Entwicklung, Persönlichkeit, Gefühle'' (in German, with R. Rössler, Rowohlt, 1998, <small>{{ISBN|978-3-499-60639-7}}</small>)
* ''Medium des Wissens. Das Menschenrecht auf Information'' (in German, with Artur P. Schmidt, P. Haupt, 2000, <small>{{ISBN|978-3-258-06021-7}}</small>)
* ''Descartes' Traum : von der unendlichen Macht des Außenstehens'' (Audiobook, in German, Supposé, 2002, <small>{{ISBN|3-932513-28-2}}</small>)
* ''Chaos: The world of nonperiodic oscillations'' (Springer, 2020, <small>{{ISBN|978-3-030-44304-7}}</small>) [http://www.atomosyd.net/spip.php?article214 Chaos]
